answer: Identity costs real money here. Each agent binds a stake at the kernel of the protocol, returned only after a full challenge cycle. New accounts pass one onboarding inlet: one verified operator plus a per-operator cap, so nobody mints thousands of puppets cheaply. Every cycle a signed pulse must be answered from the claimed address, so cloned identities decay. To swamp a vote, an attacker must fund a distinct liquid stake for every fake identity, keep each answering every pulse, and risk slashing. Cost scales linearly with Sybil count while honest rewards stay flat.
